paper.title: When Combinatorial Thompson Sampling meets Approximation Regret

settings.name_in_paper: CMAB-T (combinatorial semi-bandit with probabilistically triggered arms), independent outcomes in [0,1]
unmapped: general (possibly nonlinear, possibly infinite action space) expected reward r(A, mu) satisfying 1-norm triggering-probability-modulated bounded smoothness with constants B_i (Assumption 2)
the learner knows the action space, triggering distribution D_trig and reward function r, and has access to an (alpha-approximation) oracle
base-arm outcomes mutually independent across arms
settings.definition_quote: At round $t$, the agent selects $A_t\in \cA$ ... Then, an independent sample $\bX_t\sim \Prb_{\bX},~\bX_t\in \R^n$ is drawn and a random subset $S_t\in \cS\subset \cP([n])$ of arms are triggered ... the outcome of each triggered arm is observed ... The expected reward is of the form $r(A_t,\bmu^*)$ ... The objects $\cA,D_{\text{trig}},r$ are known to the agent.

unmapped: general (possibly nonlinear) expected reward r(A, mu) satisfying 1-norm triggering-probability-modulated bounded smoothness with constants B_i (Assumption 2)
the learner knows the action space, triggering distribution D_trig and reward function r, and has access to an (alpha-approximation) oracle
outcome vector jointly sub-Gaussian with variance proxy 1/4 (possibly correlated arms); if not independent, triggering does not depend on outcomes

symbols.B_i: smoothness constant of base arm i (Assumption 2)
symbols.Delta_i_min: minimal gap of an action that can trigger arm i
symbols.m: max number of triggerable arms of an action

conditions: Assumption 2 (1-norm triggering probability modulated bounded smoothness)
outcomes independent across arms and in [0,1]

source.label: thm:tsexact
source.quote: If $\Delta_{\min}>0$ and $p^*>0$, the policy $\pi$ described in Algorithm~\ref{algo:tsbeta} (under Assumptions~\ref{ass:approx},~\ref{ass:smooth} and~$\Prb_{\bX}=\otimes_{i\in [n]}\Prb_{X_i}$, $\bX\overset{a.s.}{\in}[0,1]^n$) or Algorithm~\ref{algo:tsgauss} (under Assumptions~\ref{ass:approx},~\ref{ass:smooth}~and \ref{ass:subgau}) has a regret of order \[R_{T,1}(\pi)=\cO\pa{\sum_{i\in [n]} \frac{B_i^2\log(m)\log(T)}{\Delta_{i,\min}}}\]

results.notes: Regret defined via mean rewards r(A,mu*), so pseudo-regret. Constant term depends exponentially on m* and on 1/p*, hidden in O. Algorithm itself does not need T, though the analysis is for fixed T.

source.quote: If $\Delta_{\min}>0$ and $p^*>0$, the policy $\pi$ described in Algorithm~\ref{algo:tsbeta} (under Assumption~\ref{reduce2exact} and~$\Prb_{\bX}=\otimes_{i\in [n]}\Prb_{X_i}$, $\bX\overset{a.s.}{\in}[0,1]^n$) or Algorithm~\ref{algo:tsgauss} (under Assumptions~\ref{ass:subgau} and~\ref{reduce2exact}) has regret of order \[R_{T,\alpha}(\pi)=\cO\pa{\sum_{i\in [n]}\frac{ \pa{ \sum_{j\in [\ell]} B_{ij}c_j }^2\log(m)\log(T)}{\Delta_{i,\min}}}.\]

results.notes: Approximation regret against alpha * optimal reward. Applies to e.g. greedy oracle for probabilistic maximum coverage / submodular maximisation, OIM, k-center, vertex cover, Max-Cut.
